title: Does a federal statute or Federal Rule govern?
shortTitle: Does a federal statute or Federal Rule govern?
summary: A scope inquiry asks whether the federal provision actually answers the disputed procedural question. A direct conflict requires a different analysis from a situation in which the state and federal provisions can operate together.
notes: Calling a state rule substantive does not by itself prove that a Federal Rule is inapplicable. Calling a federal provision procedural does not establish its precise scope.

sections.Meaning: A scope inquiry asks whether the federal provision actually answers the disputed procedural question. A direct conflict requires a different analysis from a situation in which the state and federal provisions can operate together.
sections.How to work through the question: Define the question precisely and compare the provisions. Hanna finds an unavoidable conflict over service. Walker reads Rule 3 as not deciding when the state limitations period is tolled. Stewart examines the transfer statute. After scope, assess the federal provision’s authority under the relevant standard.
